newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Police free second suspect in Hebron shooting.
newsitem.headline: Police free second suspect in Hebron shooting.

text.p: Israeli police released on Friday a second man who had been arrested in connection with Wednesday's shooting of seven Palestinians in the West Bank town of Hebron by an off-duty soldier, military sources said.
"The soldier Yuval Jibli was released from jail this afternoon," one source said. Jibli, 21, was arrested late on Wednesday on suspicion he helped gunman Noam Friedman plan the attack.
A magistrates court ordered on Thursday Friedman, who is suspected of opening fire on Palestinians in a crowded Hebron market, held for 10 days. The same court remanded Jibli for four days.
"Internal security investigations have ruled out the possibility that Noam Friedman had accomplices in his action," another source said.
Friedman, an Orthodox Jew from the Maaleh Adumim settlement in the West Bank, is suspected of attempted murder and sedition.

He told investigators he wanted to sabotage a Hebron deal to handover 80 percent of the city to Palestinian rule. Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been working to complete an elusive accord on Hebron, a flashpoint of violence.
"We are really facing a big problem in the negotiations with the Israeli side," said Palestinian minister Nabil Shaath after a weekly cabinet meeting in Gaza on Friday.
Shaath accused the United States of bias. Washington is trying to broker the long-delayed handover of 80 percent of the West Bank city of Hebron to Palestinian rule.

"I think all that is happening shows that the American position is not neutral but in many situations the Americans take a position very close to the Israeli position which makes reaching an agreement difficult," Shaath said.
"Sometimes the American co-sponsor implies that we are creating new issues as if we are delaying the negotiations as if there is a desire not to reach the liberation of Hebron," Shaath said.
